rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday term for an unpaid helper who freely provides a service.

example.english: I’m going to volunteer at a nursing home this Sunday.
example.traditional: 今個星期日我去老人院做義工。
example.jyutping: gam1 go3 sing1 kei4 jat6 ngo5 heoi3 lou5 jan4 jyun2 zou6 ji6 gung1

rows.note: Use this more formal, general term when identifying a volunteer without focusing on the everyday unpaid-helper role covered by 義工.

example.traditional: 主辦方向每位志願者致謝。
example.jyutping: zyu2 baan6 fong1 hoeng3 mui5 wai6 zi3 jyun6 ze2 zi3 ze6

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for offering to do something or offering information without being prompted.

example.english: No one wants to do it this time, so Ming will volunteer to help.
example.traditional: 今次冇人肯做，阿明就主動提出幫手。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 mou5 jan4 hang2 zou6 aa3 ming4 zau6 zyu2 dung6 tai4 ceot1 bong1 sau2

rows.note: Use this when someone steps forward and offers to take on a task, especially enthusiastically.

example.english: I volunteer to help move the tables.
example.traditional: 我自告奮勇幫手搬啲枱。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zi6 gou3 fan5 jung5 bong1 sau2 bun1 di1 toi4

rows.note: Use this when someone signs up or joins an activity of their own free will.

example.english: People can volunteer to join this workshop by signing up if they want to come.
example.traditional: 呢個工作坊係自願參加嘅，想嚟先報名。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 gung1 zok3 fong1 hai6 zi6 jyun6 caam1 gaa1 ge3 soeng2 lai4 sin1 bou3 ming4

rows.note: Use this specifically for someone who voluntarily joins the military rather than being conscripted.

example.english: They chose to serve as a volunteer soldier rather than being conscripted.
example.traditional: 佢係自己揀做志願兵，唔係畀人徵召入伍。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 zi6 gei2 gaan2 zou6 zi3 jyun6 bing1 m4 hai6 bei2 jan4 zing1 ziu1 jap6 ng5
